sources.notes: Only fiscal 2001 facts used: GO.com closure caused $878 million restructuring/impairment charges; ABC had lower ratings and weaker advertising; September 11 closures and reduced travel hurt park attendance. Disney California Adventure opened in fiscal 2001. Does not narrate fiscal 2002 totals after the April/July endpoints.
Company annual-report archive: Asian financial crisis and weaker U.S. demand left excess stock and discounting in fiscal 1998; revenue growth slowed to 4% and gross margin fell from 40.1% to 36.5%.

Retrospective fiscal 2001 discussion: new demand/supply planning system caused excess stock, shortages and late deliveries; U.S. footwear revenue fell 4.2%, international revenue grew, and net income was $589.7 million. Fiscal 2002 revenue grew 4.3% to $9.89 billion. Scenarios ending before May 2002 use only the report’s 2001 facts.

Company archive: recession and technology spending cuts followed overbuilding; fiscal 2001 revenue fell 21% to $26.5 billion and net income fell 88%, including acquisition charges. Intel introduced a 2 GHz Pentium 4 in August 2001.
